The slide subtracts `samples[i - w + 1]` instead of `samples[i - w]`, so it removes the second element of the old window rather than the one actually leaving — every window sum after the first is wrong by one element (off-by-one on the departing index).

`asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` followed by `parts = [r for r in results if isinstance(r, dict)]` silently discards failed parts, and the only guard (`if not parts`) fires when *every* part fails — so any partial failure still calls `complete_multipart_upload` with the surviving subset, producing a silently truncated object while `upload()` returns success.

`self._sem.release()` is inside the `try` block, so any `FetchError` returns without releasing the in-flight permit; after 8 failed fetches the semaphore is permanently exhausted, every worker blocks forever in `_sem.acquire()`, `frontier.join()` never completes and the crawl silently hangs instead of finishing.

The dispatched job tasks are created with `asyncio.create_task(...)` and never stored anywhere, so the event loop keeps only a weak reference to them — under GC pressure an in-flight job task can be collected mid-`await` and silently vanish, so jobs intermittently never finish and neither `mark_done` nor `mark_failed` is ever recorded.

The two per-account locks are acquired in source-then-destination order rather than a canonical global order (e.g. sorted by account id), which is not a consistent total order across transfers — a concurrent A->B and B->A pair each grab one lock and wait forever on the other, permanently deadlocking both transfers and eventually starving the 100-permit semaphore until the whole ledger wedges.

Both `EnvConfig.from_dict` (`raw.get("rollout") or None`) and `FlagConfig.from_dict` (`raw.get("rollout") or 100`) use truthiness, so an explicit `rollout: 0` — a staged-but-fully-off flag — is treated as absent and silently becomes a 100% rollout.

Money is carried as `float` on `Carrier`/`Surcharge`/`Quote` and only converted to `Decimal` at render time, so per-lb rates like 0.395 and the 0.145 fuel factor accumulate binary-float error before quantization — totals can round to a different cent than the original all-`Decimal` arithmetic.

planted_flaw: The consolidated `except Exception` unlinks the temp file on every failure, and since PartialDownload is an Exception it now deletes the `.part` file the nightly repair job was supposed to resume from.

The outer `except Exception` logs, checkpoints progress, and `return applied` normally, so a failed migration no longer raises `MigrationError` out of the function and the deploy tool sees success instead of aborting.

The backoff wraps the entire `_post_once` (debit + credit), so when the credit fails and `PostingError` is raised, `_with_backoff` retries and re-sends the non-idempotent `api.debit`, double-debiting the account.

`TransportError` subclasses `Exception`, not `OSError`, and the final failure now re-raises as `TransportError`, so the scheduler's `except OSError` no longer catches it and transient transport failures stop being rescheduled.

The `ExitStack` enters the file before the lock, so LIFO unwinding releases the lock BEFORE the file is flushed and closed, breaking the invariant and letting a reader that grabs the lock see a half-written checkpoint.

The wrapper derives the rollup key from `type(args[0]).__name__`, assuming `args[0]` is always `self`; on a plain module-level function it files timings under the first argument's type (e.g. a ledger's class) and on a classmethod it records `'type'`, corrupting the by-class buckets.

`resolve` iterates `sorted(cls._plugins, key=lambda p: p.__name__)`, which replaces definition-order precedence with alphabetical order, so `AdminRoutes` (A) still happens to win here but any pair where the broad plugin sorts first — e.g. `CatchallRoutes` vs `ZadminRoutes` — silently flips first-match-wins.

`lru_cache` on an unbound method includes `self` in the cache key and the cache lives on the function object for the process lifetime, so every per-request `PriceEngine` is held by a strong reference in the cache (never garbage-collected) and the cache is shared across all engines instead of being per-instance; `functools.cached_property` or a per-instance cache is required.

The descriptor reads and writes `obj.__dict__[self.private_name]`, but `Point` defines `__slots__` and therefore has no `__dict__`, so every `self.x = x` raises `AttributeError: 'Point' object has no attribute '__dict__'`; with slots the descriptor must use `setattr`/`getattr` into the `_x`/`_y` slots (or the owner must add `__dict__` to `__slots__`, defeating the optimization).

`functools.singledispatch` on a method dispatches on the *first* positional argument, which is `self`, so every call dispatches on the `Renderer` type and always hits the generic `TypeError` branch regardless of `node`'s type; a method needs `functools.singledispatchmethod`, which skips `self` and dispatches on the following argument.

The final `groupby(["session_id", "visitor_id"])` uses pandas' default `dropna=True`, so the ~1.8% of events with a null `visitor_id` — which the original deliberately kept via `dropna=False` — are silently dropped and their sessions vanish from the output entirely.

The `merge` has no `validate=` and the yesterday snapshot is never deduplicated, so the ~0.3% of duplicated `(sku, warehouse)` keys fan out into multiple output rows instead of the dict's last-write-wins single row, silently inflating the row count and double-counting delta_value.

The "streaming" version appends every per-chunk partial to a list and calls `pd.concat(partials)` on all of them at once at the end; for a 55GB file with high-cardinality (merchant_id, txn_date, mcc) keys the accumulated partials are themselves enormous, so peak memory is not bounded and the < 6GB ceiling is violated — it never reduces incrementally.

The vectorized `resample("15min")` drops the original's `closed="right", label="right"` and falls back to pandas' defaults (`closed="left", label="left"`), so every bin edge shifts: boundary readings land in the adjacent bin and `bin_end` labels move by 15 minutes, breaking the feature-store keys.

`first_station=("station", "first")` uses `GroupBy.first()`, which skips NaN — so an order whose earliest scan had a null station reports the next non-null station instead of the null the original `sort_values("scan_ts")["station"].iloc[0]` returned, silently erasing the untracked-first-scan signal.

`SystemClock.now()` returns `time.monotonic()`, which is an arbitrary uptime-relative float, so the epoch-second `reset_at`/`retry_after` values shipped in `X-RateLimit-Reset` become meaningless to clients (and inconsistent between gateway processes), even though every fake-clock test still passes.

`_deprecated_kwargs` warns and then `kwargs.pop(old)`s the legacy values, so `ApiClient(url, retries=5, backoff=1.0)` is silently downgraded to the default `RetryPolicy()` (3 retries, 0.5s) instead of honouring the old kwargs as required.

`DEFAULT_SETTINGS = Settings.from_env()` runs at module import, so the environment is still snapshotted (and `ANALYTICS_API_BASE`/`ANALYTICS_API_KEY` still required) the moment `analytics.client` is imported — violating the no-env-at-import constraint and still forcing `importlib.reload` for any test that sets env vars before constructing a default client.

The warning is raised inside the shared `_warn_default_change` helper with `stacklevel=2`, which attributes it to `read_table`/`read_file` in `tabular/reader.py` rather than to the caller's line (it needs `stacklevel=3` from a helper one frame deeper, or the `warnings.warn` call inlined into each public function).

`_freeze` wraps the returned data (and its nested `feature_flags`) in `MappingProxyType`, so the admin endpoint's load-bearing in-place `cfg["feature_flags"][name] = bool(on)` now raises `TypeError: 'mappingproxy' object does not support item assignment` at runtime.

The Decimals are built straight from the float arguments (`Decimal(amount)`/`Decimal(rate)`) instead of `Decimal(str(...))`, so each float's full binary-representation error is imported into the Decimal and boundary payouts round to the wrong cent.
